zh: 嗯，大概不会，因为他们可能都很脆弱，因为他们在看着对方，并且在观察对方在做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for me, I look at that situation like, I want to go for the next innovative young company who's maybe not trying to do all things for all lawyers and be more highly specialized, like GetDynasty is in the trust world.
zh: 所以对我来说，我看待那种情况就像，我想去找下一个创新的年轻公司，它也许不试图为所有律师做所有事情，并且更加高度专业化，就像 GetDynasty 在信托领域那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do something very specific.
zh: 做一些非常具体的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by the way, this has been Peter Thiel's advice is start with a niche, dominate the niche, and then grow it out.
zh: 顺便说一句，这也是 Peter Thiel 的建议，从一个细分市场开始，主导这个细分市场，然后再向外扩张。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when you're trying to take a whole ocean like the legal system, I just wonder if it's kind of contrary to Peter Thiel's advice.
zh: 所以当你试图吞下整个海洋，比如法律体系，我只是想知道这是否有点违背 Peter Thiel 的建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you worry that we just throw price out of the window?
zh: 你担心我们只是把价格抛到九霄云外吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: It seems like we've never been less price sensitive.
zh: 看起来我们要从未对价格如此不敏感。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is crazier than 2021, Jerry.
zh: 这比 2021 年更疯狂，Jerry。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm investing every single day on the ground.
zh: 我每天都在实地进行投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: I consistently have founders say, oh, you know, we're raising a hundred.
zh: 我一直有创始人说，噢，你知道，我们在融一百。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, oh, well, it's like, how much are you raising?
zh: 我就说，噢，好吧，就像，你们融多少？

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're like, we're raising a hundred.
zh: 他们就说，我们在融一百。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm like, that's the friends and family round.
zh: 我就说，那是亲友轮。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when I said to a founder the other day, we write $25 million checks, and they were like, okay, good.
zh: 就在几天前我对一个创始人的时候说，我们写 2500 万美元的支票，他们就说，好的，很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're small and collaborative.
zh: 所以你是小而协作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Have we just lost price sensitivity?
zh: 我们是不是已经失去了价格敏感度？

speaker: Unknown
en: And is that okay, given all outcomes can be trillion dollar companies?
zh: 这没问题吗，鉴于所有结果都可能是万亿美元级别的公司？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's evidence that we're still in the hype cycle, right?
zh: 这证明我们仍处于炒作周期中，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: We're in the hype cycle because expectations are beyond everyone's imagination.
zh: 我们处于炒作周期中，因为预期超出了所有人的想象。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you're saying, I'm going to be a trillion dollar company, my opening round is a hundred million or something, or even a billion, whatever the valuation is are, you just recognize and you have to look in your head and look at the people that are going to take that money.
zh: 所以如果你说，我要成为一家万亿美元的公司，我的首轮是一亿或者什么，甚至十亿，不管估值是多少，你只是要认识到，并且你必须在脑海中审视，还要看看那些要拿这笔钱的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're going to recognize that, has that number been well thought out or are they just doing it because the market's doing it?
zh: 而且你会认识到，那个数字是经过深思熟虑的，还是他们这样做只是因为市场在这样做？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I would argue that it looks like Anthropic and OpenAI, those crazy mega rounds, you know, at $100 billion, $150 billion might actually have been cheap.
zh: 我认为对于 Anthropic 和 OpenAI，那些疯狂的巨额轮次，你知道，1000 亿美元、1500 亿美元，实际上可能很便宜。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think Gavin Baker probably believes that and others believe that.
zh: 我的意思是，我认为 Gavin Baker 可能相信这一点，其他人也相信。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so for a few companies, yeah.
zh: 所以对于少数公司来说，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But how many trillion dollar companies are we going to have?
zh: 但是我们将会有多少家万亿美元的公司？

speaker: Unknown
en: Discernment, again, is necessary here to decide what really can have this sort of hyperscale type growth associated with it and which ones are going to be also RANs or a little more of a slower growth opportunity.
zh: 识辨力，在这里又是必要的，以决定哪些真正具有这种超规模类型的增长，而哪些将成为 RANs 或稍微更慢一些的增长机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we need to sort out those a little better.
zh: 我们需要稍微更好地把它们分拣出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's slower growth venture anymore, Jerry.
zh: 这不再是缓慢增长的风投了，Jerry。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we look at fireworks, you know, it's three and a half years to a billion.
zh: 如果我们看看 fireworks，你知道，它用了三年半时间达到 10 亿。

speaker: Unknown
en: It'll be four years to two billion if they hit end of year targets this year.
zh: 如果他们今年能达到年底目标，那将需要四年时间达到 20 亿。

speaker: Unknown
en: Four years to two billion.
zh: 四年达到 20 亿。

speaker: Unknown
en: Jerry, do you remember when it was slack 18 months to 10 million and we were like, wow, wow.
zh: Jerry，你还记得以前是 Slack 18 个月达到 1000 万，那时候我们就像，哇，哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in the case of fireworks, look, they're benefiting because of OpenAI and Anthropic.
zh: 我认为在 fireworks 这个案例中，看，他们受益于 OpenAI 和 Anthropic。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are the next level.
zh: 他们是下一层。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now with open source taking off, they're benefiting from that.
zh: 现在随着开源腾飞，他们受益于此。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so they ride on the shoulders of these model builders and they're the next layer that needs to get developed.
zh: 所以他们骑在这些模型构建者的肩膀上，并且他们是需要被开发的下一层。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so they can scale right behind that.
zh: 所以他们可以紧随其后进行扩张。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you're somebody else, like say in the app layer, I'm just not buying that.
zh: 但如果你是其他人，比如在应用层，我根本不相信。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not buying it.
zh: 我不信。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not buying it for the legal and I'm not buying it for the app layers yet.
zh: 对于法律领域我不信，对于应用层我也不信。

speaker: Unknown
en: But for infrastructure, absolutely.
zh: 但对于基础设施，绝对相信。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I get killed for this.
zh: 但我因此被骂得很惨。

speaker: Unknown
en: I say publicly, triple, triple, double, doubles.
zh: 我公开说，三倍，三倍，翻倍，翻倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: Dad, you remember this.
zh: Dad，你记得这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Am I glib and my kid, you are a product of a cycle?
zh: 我是不是轻率了，我的孩子，你是周期的产物？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or is this just a new expectation level for venture?
zh: 还是这只是风投的新预期水平？

speaker: Unknown
en: You are glib.
zh: 你很油嘴滑舌。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes, not all the time, but right now you are, yeah.
zh: 有时候，不是一直，但现在你是，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would argue that general statements don't apply here.
zh: 我会争辩说笼统的陈述在这里不适用。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to be highly specific.
zh: 你必须非常具体。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look at Anthropic and you look at what they've done, Anthropic and OpenAI, it's never been done in the history of the world.
zh: 如果你看看 Anthropic 并看看他们做了什么，Anthropic 和 OpenAI，这在世界历史上从未有过。

speaker: Unknown
en: It shows the importance of the time.
zh: 它展示了这个时代的重要性。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we are definitely, if we look through the history of venture, in a completely different era.
zh: 所以我们绝对是，如果我们回顾风投的历史，处于一个完全不同的时代。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the frontier model companies have done something extraordinary in the history of the world.
zh: 并且前沿模型公司做了一些在世界历史上非同寻常的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, this is definitely on the level of inventing fire, electricity, whatever you want to call it.
zh: 我的意思是，这绝对达到了发明火、电，或者无论你想叫它什么的水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's truly extraordinary what the frontier model companies have done.
zh: 前沿模型公司所做的事情真正非同寻常。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've lit the match to AI.
zh: 他们点燃了 AI 的火柴。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the companies that can follow right on top of them and not get killed by them, but can grow and solve more infrastructure problems and help create an ecosystem around the model companies, those guys, they deserve those economics.
zh: 那些能紧随其后并且不被他们扼杀，而是能成长并解决更多基础设施问题并帮助围绕模型公司创建生态系统的公司，这些人，他们配得上那些经济利益。

speaker: Unknown
en: Other categories?
zh: 其他类别？

speaker: Unknown
en: No way.
zh: 没门。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, for example, neoclouds.
zh: 比如，举个例子，neoclouds。

speaker: Unknown
en: No way.
zh: 没门。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't buy it.
zh: 我不买账。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think some, one or two of those neoclouds are going to end up dominating, and a lot of them, at least half of them, are going to go away.
zh: 我认为其中一些，那些 neoclouds 中的一两个最终会占据主导地位，而他们中的很多，至少一半，将会消失。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're going to go away with massive amounts of money being burned as part of it.
zh: 并且他们将会伴随着巨额的资金烧毁而消失。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does the model routing layer carry enough value to you to be independent?
zh: 模型路由层对你来说是否具有足够的价值从而独立存在？

speaker: Unknown
en: My opinion is OpenRouter has massive amounts of transactions because people are basically lazy, right?
zh: 我的看法是 OpenRouter 有巨大的交易量，因为人们基本上是懒惰的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It was easy.
zh: 它很简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, I need to connect to this model.
zh: 好的，我需要连接到这个模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm just going to use OpenRouter.
zh: 我就直接用 OpenRouter。

speaker: Unknown
en: And OpenRouter charges 5% on top of that, which is a crazy amount of money.
zh: 而且 OpenRouter 在此基础上收取 5% 的费用，这是一笔疯狂的钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not going to last.
zh: 这不会长久。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're going to see exchanges.
zh: 你会看到交易所。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a blockchain company called Akinaki that has just launched Dodex on their mainnet.
zh: 有一家区块链公司叫 Akinaki 刚刚在他们的主网上推出了 Dodex。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this thing is an exchange to go out and buy inference.
zh: 这个东西是一个用来出去购买推理的交易所。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as part of that, all the model routing is done for you.
zh: 作为其中的一部分，所有的模型路由都为你完成了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think you're going to see multiple opportunities to an open router type product where people that are hosting the models themselves will provide, you know, through an exchange, an easy way to acquire the inference and the need for an open router type product and particularly paying the 5% markup for the inference won't matter, right?
zh: 所以我认为你会看到像 open router 类型产品的多种机会，那些自己托管模型的人将通过交易所提供一种简单的方式来获取推理，并且对 open router 类型产品的需求，特别是为推理支付 5% 的加价将无关紧要，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because that's what those things do.
zh: 因为这就是那些东西所做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're not necessary long term.
zh: 它们长期来看不是必需的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you're on the board of OpenRouter and the $10 billion acquisition comes through, what do you say?
zh: 所以如果你是 OpenRouter 董事会的成员，并且 100 亿美元的收购案通过了，你会说什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: You say, fuck yeah, this is great.
zh: 你会说，去他妈的，太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like a lot of people, you take the money when you can.
zh: 像很多人一样，你在能拿钱的时候就拿钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Credit to OpenRouter.
zh: 归功于 OpenRouter。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're there early.
zh: 他们来得很早。

speaker: Unknown
en: Developers didn't see another alternative.
zh: 开发者没有看到另一个替代方案。

speaker: Unknown
en: They could just go to there, go to the API, and they're willing to pay 5% markup to get their inference.
zh: 他们可以直接去那里，去 API，并且他们愿意支付 5% 的加价来获得他们的推理。

speaker: Unknown
en: And guess what?
zh: 你猜怎么着？

speaker: Unknown
en: Shame on the enterprises for letting them burn all that money.
zh: 企业们真丢脸，任由他们烧掉所有的钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a huge amount of money.
zh: 那是一笔巨款。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think that you're going to see a big disruption in that model in the next three, four, five months.
zh: 所以我认为你会看到该模式在未来三四五个月内出现巨大的颠覆。

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, not just Akinaki, but Venice, Venice IO is doing that.
zh: 实际上，不只是 Akinaki，Venice，Venice IO 正在这样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's two or three other guys that are now in the process of building exchanges that you can go directly, get the inference you need without paying the 5% markup.
zh: 还有另外两三个人现在正在建立交易所的过程中，你可以直接去那里，获得你需要的推理，而无需支付 5% 的加价。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you very accurately said about kind of where we are today, the potential dislocation of excitement, dislocation due to external affairs, and then the re-blossoming of an ecosystem, so to speak.
zh: 我认为你非常准确地说到了我们今天所处的位置，潜在的热情错位，因外部事务导致的错位，然后可以说是生态系统的重新开花。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think about that and you advise me as a venture investor deploying, say, your money today, what would you say to me?
zh: 如果你考虑到这一点，并且你作为一位风投投资者建议我部署，比如说，你今天的钱，你会对我说什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Play the game on the field, Bill Gurley style, be mindful, don't spunk cash into Neo Labs at a billion dollars pre for one person out of OpenAI.
zh: 在球场上比赛，Bill Gurley 风格，保持警惕，不要把现金撒给 Neo Labs，以 10 亿美元的前估值投给一个从 OpenAI 出来的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: What would you say to me?
zh: 你会对我说什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, Bill's on the board of the Santa Fe Institute with me.
zh: 嗯，Bill 和我一起在圣塔菲研究所的董事会。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, his guidance is pretty smart.
zh: 我的意思是，他的指导相当明智。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's pretty much on point with a lot of things with venture capital.
zh: 在很多关于风险投资的事情上，他基本上都很切题。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I would suggest is you look for impact.
zh: 我会建议你去寻找影响力。

speaker: Unknown
en: You look for people that are going to be just, they're just way different than anyone else.
zh: 你要寻找那些将会就是，他们就是与其他任何人都截然不同的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you look at them and you realize it's not that they want to build this business, it's that they have to build this business.
zh: 当你审视他们时，你会意识到并不是他们想要建立这项业务，而是他们不得不建立这项业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you find that in a person and you recognize that they have the commitment to it, because the commitment to it is all in.
zh: 如果你在一个人身上发现了这一点，并且你认识到他们对此有承诺，因为这种承诺就是全力以赴。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no other option.
zh: 没有其他选项。

speaker: Unknown
en: Look for that and look for the fact that what they're going to do has impact if they do it.
zh: 寻找这一点，并且寻找这样一个事实，即他们要做的事情如果有做成的话，会有影响力。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you review the founders you've worked with, where was that most obviously striking?
zh: 当你回顾你合作过的创始人时，哪一点最明显地令人印象深刻？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's rare, right?
zh: 这很罕见，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because you could say all the founder-driven Mag7 companies would qualify, right?
zh: 因为你可以说所有由创始人驱动的 Mag7 公司都符合条件，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, Elon, Jensen, Zuckerberg, they all qualify for that definition.
zh: 我的意思是，Elon、Jensen、Zuckerberg，他们都符合那个定义。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you look at these other companies that you say, well, Fireworks looks to be like that.
zh: 但是你看这些其他公司，你会说，嗯，Fireworks 看起来像是那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: A to B is definitely like that.
zh: A to B 绝对是那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: The founder, Vignan, he's absolutely going to do it.
zh: 创始人，Vignan，他绝对会做成这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no question in my mind.
zh: 我对此毫无疑问。

speaker: Unknown
en: Avin, this guy came out of Meta as well.
zh: Avin，这家伙也是从 Meta 出来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: His name is Saadi Khan.
zh: 他的名字是 Saadi Khan。

speaker: Unknown
en: But Alkosha said this is one of the best CEOs ever seen.
zh: 但 Alkosha 说这是见过的最好的 CEO 之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Vinod was one of the best CEOs building Sun.
zh: 而 Vinod 是组建 Sun 的最好的 CEO 之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when someone says that, you take it seriously.
zh: 所以当有人那样说时，你会很认真对待。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think we see a compression in like liquidity timelines?
zh: 你认为我们会看到像流动性时间表这样的压缩吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: We have Cursor scaling to 60 billion sale in four years.
zh: 我们有 Cursor 在四年内扩展到 600 亿的销售额。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do we see actually venture cycles get shorter in this environment given companies grow faster?
zh: 鉴于公司增长更快，在这个环境中我们是否真的看到风险投资周期变短？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think what Cursor did, because the team is really smart, is they pivoted out of the IDE space.
zh: 我认为 Cursor 所做的，因为团队真的很聪明，是他们从 IDE 领域转型了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they pivoted.
zh: 他们转型了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in that pivot, they convinced Elon that they could build models.
zh: 在那次转型中，他们说服了 Elon 他们可以构建模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: They hadn't proved it yet, but they convinced him that they knew enough to do it.
zh: 他们还没有证明这一点，但他们说服了他，让他们知道自己足够了解能做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Elon was pretty desperate to solve his problem with xAI.
zh: 而 Elon 当时非常迫切地想解决他在 xAI 上的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it was a great fit.
zh: 所以这是一个完美的契合。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they got the $60 billion.
zh: 然后他们拿到了那 600 亿。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you hit the bid.
zh: 所以你接了这个报价。

speaker: Unknown
en: If OpenRouter gets a $10 billion bid from Stripe, you take it.
zh: 如果 OpenRouter 收到来自 Stripe 的 100 亿报价，你会接受的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think those are not the norm.
zh: 我认为那些并非常态。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are events that are happening because the board and the management realizes, hey, maybe what we've built isn't a decade company.
zh: 那些事件正在发生，因为董事会和管理层意识到，嘿，也许我们建立的东西并不是一家十年的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe this is something that we need to move out of and we take the win for what we had.
zh: 也许这是我们需要退出的东西，我们就拿走我们已经赢得的收益。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I had a few companies back in the day that I wish had done that.
zh: 过去我有几家公司，我希望它们当时那样做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Flipboard was one of them and I wish Flipboard had taken the billion dollar exit, but they didn't.
zh: Flipboard 就是其中之一，我希望 Flipboard 当时接受了那个 10 亿美元的退出，但他们没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: What happened there?
zh: 那里发生了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: They had a billion-dollar asset on the table.
zh: 他们桌面上有 10 亿美元的资产。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, they had an opportunity, yeah.
zh: 嗯，他们有一个机会，是的。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我认为数据本身比人们认为的要难得多，在获取、清洗和部署方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you feel about data providing companies as a commodity or as a valuable asset?
zh: 你觉得作为商品或有价值资产的数据提供公司怎么样？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, data keeps changing.
zh: 嗯，数据不断变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the thing about data is it's not static.
zh: 所以关于数据的事情是它不是静止的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's, of course, value to context, right?
zh: 当然，上下文有价值，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Data gives you the context and memory, right?
zh: 数据给你上下文和记忆，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I do think that if you're an enterprise business, your data, the way you do it, will be different than the way someone else... Take hamburger companies, right?
zh: 所以我确实认为如果你是一家企业，你的数据，你的使用方式，将与别人的方式不同……拿汉堡公司来说，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Shake Shack's data is going to be utilized differently than say Burger King will do it or McDonald's.
zh: Shake Shack 的数据的使用方式将与 Burger King 或 McDonald's 的做法不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I do think that there's going to be highly unique use cases for data that is really important, but you have to have a system where the data continues to evolve and change and the underlying utilization of it can change as the data changes.
zh: 所以我确实认为数据将会有真正重要的高度独特的用例，但你必须有一个系统，让数据持续进化和变化，并且它的底层利用可以随着数据变化而改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think I buy Lin's thesis that you'll have specialized models for companies and part of the training for those models will require additional surplus data.
zh: 我想我认同 Lin 的论点，你将拥有为公司定制的专用模型，那些模型训练的一部分将需要额外的剩余数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you'll see the likes of McCaw go from purely selling to frontier models to selling to enterprises and even mid-market who need specialized data that they might not have.
zh: 然后你会看到像 McCaw 这样的公司从纯粹向前沿模型销售转向向企业甚至中端市场销售，这些客户需要他们可能没有的专用数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that massively opens the TAM.
zh: 那极大地打开了 TAM。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the $200 billion opportunity.
zh: 那就是那个 2000 亿美元的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right now, models are essentially task-driven to a large degree.
zh: 现在，模型在很大程度上本质上是任务驱动的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Frontier models are doing some levels of creativity, but we really want it to be deep creativity, like go solve climate change.
zh: 前沿模型正在做某种程度的创造力，但我们真的希望它是深度创造力，比如去解决气候变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're going to need a diversity of intelligence.
zh: 你将需要智能的多样性。

speaker: Unknown
en: You think about board levels and you think about management teams.
zh: 你想想董事会层面，你想想管理团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need diversity of intelligence to be able to solve really difficult problems.
zh: 你需要智能的多样性才能解决真正困难的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the market is going to change from, let's just solve tasks and do it a great way.
zh: 所以市场将从，让我们只解决任务并且很好地完成它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's do minimal creativity with writing and visual arts to being, oh, we really need a lot of diversity of intelligence to be creative enough to solve the problems that matter and the problems that we're going to get paid for.
zh: 让我们在写作和视觉艺术方面做极少的创造力，变成，哦，我们真的需要很多智能的多样性才能足够有创造力去解决重要的问题和我们将为此获得报酬的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I find everything that we talk about today so exciting.
zh: 我觉得我们要谈论的一切都非常令人兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I just have one pullback in my mind, which is just a lot of wise people say you always overestimate what you can do in a year and underestimate what you can do in 10.
zh: 然后我脑子里只有一个顾虑，就是很多明智的人说你总是高估你一年能做的事，而低估你 10 年能做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that the case here?
zh: 是这种情况吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Am I massively getting ahead of myself when I think about a lot of what we've spoken about and actually calm down kiddo, it takes longer than you think.
zh: 当我想到了我们谈论的很多事情时，我是不是太超前了，实际上冷静点孩子，这比你想的要花更长时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: My feeling is that continuous learning, it feels like it's two to three years away.
zh: 我的感觉是持续学习，感觉它还有两三年。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe it's 10 years away.
zh: 也许还有 10 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't know.
zh: 我们不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, we've been thinking we're on the cusp of solving cancer for the past 15 years.
zh: 我的意思是，我们认为我们在过去 15 年里一直处于解决癌症的临界点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we got a little bump with the new sort of drugs like Keytruda to do cancer solving problems with the immune system.
zh: 随着像 Keytruda 这样的新药出现，我们获得了一些小 bump（波动/提升），利用免疫系统来解决癌症问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for joining us today.
zh: 感谢你今天加入我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, from that small sample.
zh: 你知道的，从那个小样本来看。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so learning from small samples is starting to happen, but when they actually become robust enough to be useful, I don't know.
zh: 因此从小样本中学习正在开始发生，但它们何时真正变得足够稳健以变得有用，我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my feeling is these things take a breakthrough from where we are.
zh: 而我的感觉是，这些事情需要在我们当前位置的基础上实现突破。

speaker: Unknown
en: And just like with cancer, we need more of a breakthrough.
zh: 就像癌症一样，我们需要更多的突破。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the complexity that they're trying to solve is huge.
zh: 它们试图解决的复杂性是巨大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm not going to bet against them, but I would say what could send us into the valley of disillusionment is
zh: 所以我不会赌输他们，但我认为可能会让我们进入幻灭低谷的是

speaker: Unknown
en: A combination of a global financial event and a failure for the models to continue to grow and evolve.
zh: 全球金融事件与模型未能继续增长和演变的结合。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're gonna get to a place that if we don't solve SAPL efficient models and we don't solve continuous learning, we're gonna feel like, hey, our inflated expectations are somehow not being met.
zh: 我们将到达这样一个地步，如果我们不解决 SAPL 高效模型，并且我们不解决持续学习，我们会感觉，嘿，我们的膨胀期望没有以某种方式被满足。

speaker: Unknown
en: Jerry, I'd love to do a quick fire with you because I could talk to you all day.
zh: Jerry，我想和你来个快速问答（quick fire），因为我可以和你聊一整天。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who goes out first, OpenAI or Anthropic?
zh: 谁先出局，OpenAI 还是 Anthropic？

speaker: Unknown
en: It appears like Anthropic.
zh: 看起来像是 Anthropic。

speaker: Unknown
en: Over or under, NVIDIA will be a $10 trillion company in five years?
zh: 超过还是低于，NVIDIA 将在五年内成为一家价值 10 万亿美元的公司？

speaker: Unknown
en: Over.
zh: 超过。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is it so mispriced then, right now?
zh: 那为什么现在的定价如此错误呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's been flat for the last 12 months despite numbers going through the roof.
zh: 尽管数字直冲云霄，它在过去 12 个月里一直是 flat（持平）的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't get it.
zh: 我不明白。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's because the market doesn't go like a rocket ship forever.
zh: 我认为这是因为市场不会永远像火箭飞船一样上涨。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're going to have these plateaus.
zh: 你会遇到这些 plateaus（高原期/平台期）。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that there are areas of things not really accelerating as fast as you think it is.
zh: 我认为有些领域的加速速度并没有你想象的那么快。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't know because right now there's these circular transactions that are obfuscating real growth in the market because the hyperscalers are sort of trying to get ahead of the game.
zh: 我们不知道，因为现在存在这些 circular transactions（循环交易），它们掩盖了市场的实际增长，因为超大规模厂商（hyperscalers）正试图抢占先机。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we don't know.
zh: 但我们不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I mean, demand is going to have a lot to do with people having money in their pocket.
zh: 你知道的，我的意思是，需求将与人们口袋里的钱有很大关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you have a 10%, 15% dislocation in the markets, people are going to feel poor.
zh: 如果你在市场上有 10%、15% 的 dislocation（错位/震荡），人们会感到贫穷。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's going to affect the credit markets.
zh: 这将影响信贷市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's going to affect everything.
zh: 这将影响一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's going to affect demand.
zh: 这将影响需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: It always does.
zh: 一直都是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can't believe I'm about to say this to you, Jerry, but fuck it, we've known each other a while.
zh: 我不敢相信我要对你说这句话，Jerry，但管它呢（fuck it），我们认识有一段时间了。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the UK, we have a game called Shag, Marry, Kill, okay?
zh: 在英国，我们有一个游戏叫 Shag, Marry, Kill，好吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to apply it to three companies, and the application is Kill is short, Shag is buy quick, but you'll probably flip it, and Marry is you're in it for the long term.
zh: 我要把它应用到三家公司，应用方式是：Kill 是做空，Shag 是快进快出（买），但你可能会 flip it（反手/做差价），Marry 是你长期持有。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've got Meta, you've got Google, and you've got Microsoft.
zh: 你有 Meta，你有 Google，还有 Microsoft。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to say because of the scale, I'm going to say long term for all of them.
zh: 我要说因为规模的原因，我要说这三家都是长期。

speaker: Unknown
en: No.
zh: 不。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really?
zh: 真的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's why.
zh: 原因如下。

speaker: Unknown
en: When Meta's got 2 billion users with all their things, when Google's got 2 billion users with all their things, there's a kind of stability in that because consumers are really slow to accept new changes and things.
zh: 当 Meta 拥有 20 亿用户以及他们所有的东西，当 Google 拥有 20 亿用户以及他们所有的东西时，这里有一种稳定性，因为消费者接受新变化和事物真的很慢。

speaker: Unknown
en: So because of those two companies having such a substantial consumer business,
zh: 正因为这两家公司拥有如此庞大的消费者业务，

speaker: Unknown
en: And Microsoft's consumer business is good too.
zh: 而且 Microsoft 的消费者业务也不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: It kind of acts like a buffer, a stabilizer that gives them time to catch up.
zh: 它充当了一种缓冲、稳定器，给了他们追赶的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, let's face it, all three of them have failed on the coding agent side, but I don't know if they're going to fail forever.
zh: 我的意思是，面对现实吧，这三家在 coding agent（编码智能体）方面都失败了，但我不知道他们是否会永远失败。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you have to say this mass customer base gives them this incredible time to catch up with problems.
zh: 我认为你必须承认，这个庞大的客户群体给了他们这个不可思议的时间来追赶问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's why they're going to be trillions of dollar companies for at least a decade.
zh: 这就是为什么他们至少在未来十年内仍将是价值数万亿美元的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: They may not be as important as they are today.
zh: 他们可能不如今天这么重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not the question you ask.
zh: 那不是你问的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as an economic buyer, would I hold their stock for long term?
zh: 但作为经济买家，我会长期持有他们的股票吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I would.
zh: 是的，我会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even Microsoft?
zh: 即使是 Microsoft？

speaker: Unknown
en: No model, relatively shitty AI products.
zh: 没有模型，相对糟糕的 AI 产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'd still be a buy.
zh: 你仍然会是一个买入。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, here's why.
zh: 是的，原因如下。

speaker: Unknown
en: They control communication for the global enterprises.
zh: 他们控制着全球企业的通信。

speaker: Unknown
en: Microsoft email, as dumb as it is, I mean, Exchange, whatever you want to call it, that's not going away.
zh: 微软的电子邮件，尽管它很蠢，我是说，Exchange，不管你想叫它什么，它都不会消失。

speaker: Unknown
en: That thing is a money machine that cannot change.
zh: 那东西是一台无法改变的赚钱机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: It cannot just disappear.
zh: 它不可能就这样消失。

speaker: Unknown
en: By the way, you know, what's really interesting, we talked about the speed of AI and stuff.
zh: 顺便说一下，你知道，真正有趣的是，我们讨论了 AI 的速度之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: They won't be able to control agent communication.
zh: 他们将无法控制智能体通信。

speaker: Unknown
en: Human communication, that's not going away.
zh: 人类通信，那不会消失。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're going to be able to monetize that forever.
zh: 而且他们将永远能够从中变现。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't get rid of it.
zh: 你无法摆脱它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not like it's your cable system at home where you can say, fine, I don't need Infinity anymore.
zh: 这不像你家里的有线电视系统，你可以说，行，我不需要 Infinity 了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Get rid of it.
zh: 把它摆脱掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're not getting rid of Microsoft anytime soon.
zh: 你不会很快摆脱微软。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to be around.
zh: 它会一直存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sadly, Facebook is the same.
zh: 遗憾的是，Facebook 也是一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're not going to get rid of it anytime soon.
zh: 你不会很快摆脱它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And these guys have built these kind of businesses because of the scale that supports their underlying business.
zh: 而这些人建立这些业务是因为规模支持了他们的底层业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the consumer is, in my humble opinion, the thing that's keeping those companies afloat more than anything.
zh: 而消费者，依我看，是支撑这些公司的最重要的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You got a short one of the Mach 7, which you would... Well, it would be Meta.
zh: 你做空了 Mach 7 中的一个，你会……嗯，那就是 Meta。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we met her because that's the one that may become boring.
zh: 我们做空了它，因为那个可能会变得无聊。

speaker: Unknown
en: It may become like a telephone company.
zh: 它可能会变成一家电话公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it'll just be this malaise, like owning an AT&T or something.
zh: 我是说，它只会是这种萎靡不振，就像拥有 AT&T 或什么东西一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what you kind of think about it.
zh: 这就是你看待它的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I push back.
zh: 所以我反驳。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the largest ads business in the world.
zh: 它是世界上最大的广告业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's got WhatsApp and it's got Instagram.
zh: 它拥有 WhatsApp，它拥有 Instagram。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, WhatsApp, I mean, again, they control human communication on WhatsApp in a very meaningful way.
zh: 是的，WhatsApp，我是说，同样，他们以非常有意义的方式控制着 WhatsApp 上的人类通信。

speaker: Unknown
en: They haven't monetized it yet, but those users, they're going to find ways to keep the users.
zh: 他们还没有变现它，但那些用户，他们将找到留住用户的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: You got 2 billion plus, maybe there'll be 3 billion in five years.
zh: 你有 20 多亿，也许五年内会有 30 亿。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know, we got half the world using your application.
zh: 我不知道，我们让世界上半数人使用你的应用程序。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sorry.
zh: 抱歉。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's something that's stable.
zh: 那是一些稳定的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a stable thing.
zh: 那是一个稳定的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can't say.
zh: 我不能说。

speaker: Unknown
en: It might be boring to just generate dividends out to you.
zh: 只是给你派生股息可能会很无聊。

speaker: Unknown
en: So as an economic buyer, you don't necessarily always need growth.
zh: 所以作为一个经济买家，你不一定总是需要增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can take big fat dividends and just punch the coupon.
zh: 你可以获得巨额的股息，然后剪息票。

speaker: Unknown
en: At least for the next five years, it's going to be considered a safe haven.
zh: 至少在未来五年，它将被视为避风港。

speaker: Unknown
en: The Mag7 is the Mag7 because people say, hey, I'll put my money there.
zh: Mag7 之所以是 Mag7，是因为人们说，嘿，我会把钱放在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I might be underwater for a year or two or less of a return than I had.
zh: 我可能会在水下待一年两年，或者回报比我预期的要少。

speaker: Unknown
en: But long term, those things are going to be there and they're going to benefit with every positive cycle in the markets.
zh: 但从长远来看，这些东西会一直存在，并且会随着市场中每一个积极的周期受益。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is Apple's AI strategy unforgivable mistakes, or is it genius patience waiting to see how a developing ecosystem plays out?
zh: 苹果的 AI 策略是不可饶恕的错误，还是天才般的耐心，等待观察一个发展中生态系统如何演变？

speaker: Unknown
en: The answer to that is something that is going to be hard to know.
zh: 那个问题的答案将很难知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'd have to go sit down with Tim Cook now that he's retired.
zh: 我们得去坐下来和 Tim Cook 谈谈，既然他已经退休了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe he'd tell us.
zh: 也许他会告诉我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the culture around AI at Apple?
zh: 苹果围绕 AI 的文化是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: How are they thinking about it?
zh: 他们是如何思考它的？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are they doing in there?
zh: 他们在里面做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I know they're using Claude Code, huge, massive Claude Code customer, but how are they thinking about it?
zh: 你知道，我知道他们在用 Claude Code，巨大的、大型的 Claude Code 客户，但他们是怎么思考它的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do they have anything innovative to say?
zh: 他们有什么创新的说法吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Have they been intelligent, watchful observers?
zh: 他们是聪明的、敏锐的观察者吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or are they just dumb consumers?
zh: 还是说他们只是愚蠢的消费者？

speaker: Unknown
en: If they're consuming, sorry, they're in big trouble.
zh: 如果他们是在消费，抱歉，他们有大麻烦了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're going to suffer.
zh: 他们会遭殃的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if they're watchful observers and they've got something up their sleeve, then we could be surprised by them.
zh: 但如果他们是敏锐的观察者并且他们袖里有乾坤，那么他们可能会让我们感到惊讶。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which PE firm will navigate the next five years best?
zh: 哪家私募股权公司将在未来五年中驾驭得最好？

speaker: Unknown
en: Ooh, that's not fair.
zh: 噢，这不公平。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a tough question.
zh: 那是个很难的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wouldn't want to make that bet.
zh: 我不想下那个赌注。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which will navigate the worst?
zh: 哪一家会驾驭得最差？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I don't know who's worse, but my company Insight, they have a very small PE portfolio.
zh: 嗯，我不知道谁更差，但我公司 Insight，他们有一个非常小的 PE 投资组合。

speaker: Unknown
en: Very, very small.
zh: 非常、非常小。

speaker: Unknown
en: It almost doesn't even matter.
zh: 它几乎甚至不重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think I feel the best about them long term because they've been really intelligent about how they deploy the capital there.
zh: 所以我认为我对他们的长期感觉最好，因为他们在那里部署资本方面真的很聪明。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the people that are all in on PE all the time, I just don't know about that.
zh: 但对于那些一直全押在 PE 上的人，我只是不太清楚那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think they're highly at risk to any kind of financial dislocation.
zh: 我认为他们对任何一种金融动荡都处于高度风险之中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which venture investor do you think has fared most well in the transition to an AI world?
zh: 你认为哪位风投投资者在向 AI 世界转型的过程中表现最好？
